rationale: Retain Cordelio Power as a historical acquired platform, but end CPP Investments' direct ownership when Pattern Energy's share-based acquisition closed on April 1, 2026. Pattern integrated Cordelio's core assets, pipeline and team, while CPP's continuing exposure is represented only on the canonical Pattern Energy record. Correct Cordelio's canonical geography and headquarters, its historical 100% CPP stake, and the acquisition timeline without inferring dissolution of the surviving legal entities.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Cordelio Power was a Toronto-headquartered wind, solar and energy-storage platform operating in Canada and the United States. CPP Investments wholly owned the business from its June 29, 2018 entry until Pattern Energy's share-based acquisition closed on April 1, 2026. Pattern acquired approximately 1,550 MW across 16 operating or construction projects, most of Cordelio's U.S. development portfolio and the Cordelio team; Cordelio is therefore retained as a historical acquired company subordinate to Pattern, not as a separate active CPP Investments PortCo. CPP's continuing exposure is represented through its 69.1% ownership of Pattern. BrightNight separately announced on April 21, 2026 that it had acquired Cordelio's interest in a 6 GW development joint venture, a partial asset-level divestiture rather than a second company-level exit. Public sources reviewed do not establish the exact surviving merger entity, so dissolution is not inferred.

set.event: Cordelio Power was established as CPP Investments' renewable-power platform.
